summary: Every condition must be inspected and every cell of the required k by k returned matrix must be materialized, so the graph-and-output upper bound matches the combined input and output lower bound.

optimality.argument: A correct algorithm must inspect all r plus c directed constraints because any one may introduce a cycle or required precedence, and producing a k by k matrix requires writing k squared output cells. Two linear graph traversals followed by matrix initialization meet those costs.

replacement_checks.evidence: Changing an unread condition can make an acyclic instance cyclic, while the explicit return value always contains k squared cells.
Kahn traversal visits each value and condition once in each graph, then each matrix cell is initialized once.
Authored cases cover valid alternate layouts, duplicate edges, unconstrained values, and cycles in either dimension; the semantic validator checks placements rather than exact layout equality.
